Encrypted Vault

Keep your passwords, notes and secret codes in one safe place, on every device you sign in on. They’re locked on your device with a passphrase only you know — I can’t open them, and neither can anyone who breaks into my server.

Zero-knowledge — encrypted on your device Free account

The vault needs my server, which isn’t reachable right now.

A private place for your secrets

Logins, notes and API keys — encrypted in your browser with a passphrase only you know. I store scrambled data I can’t read, and sync it to every device you sign in on.

Sign in Create a free account

Step 1 of 2

Choose a vault passphrase

It encrypts everything in your vault. It’s separate from your account password, and I never see it — so I can’t reset it for you.

At least 10 characters. A few random words work well.

Step 2 of 2

Save your recovery key

If you ever forget your passphrase, this key is the only other way into your vault. Store it somewhere safe and offline — a password manager, or printed on paper.

Your vault is locked

Only you can open it

  • Everything is locked on your device with a passphrase only you know — before it’s saved.
  • I only store scrambled data. Even someone who broke into my server couldn’t read it.
  • It locks itself after 10 minutes without use.

Keep two things safe

Your vault passphrase and your recovery key each open the vault on their own. If you lose both, nobody can get your data back — not even me. That’s the price of real privacy.

How it works

  1. 1Make your vaultChoose a passphrase only you know.
  2. 2Add your loginsPasswords, notes and codes — locked on your device.
  3. 3Open it anywhereSign in on any device and unlock it with your passphrase.

Why can’t you open my vault?

Most online “vaults” keep the keys themselves, so they can read what you store. Here, the key is made and kept on your own device. If my database ever leaked, all anyone would find is scrambled data.

Turn on two-factor sign-in too, so nobody can even reach your vault without your phone.

For the technical folks

Your passphrase is turned into a key with 600,000 rounds of PBKDF2 in the browser; every item is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it leaves your device. A random 256-bit vault key is wrapped by both the passphrase key and the recovery key.
